extracted.intended_audience: performers, comedians, comedy students, and general readers interested in humor techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on using timing (intonation, rhythm, pauses, pacing) in comedic performance across stage, screen, and stand-up to maximize humorous effect. Describes specific timing devices (beats, pregnant pause, pacing) and how delivery and audience interaction shape timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of intonation, rhythm, cadence, tempo, and beat
rubrics_metrics.description: A performer's joke delivery as they interact with an audience using intonation, rhythm, cadence, tempo, and beat to guide the comedic narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pacing of delivery can change a joke's effect or meaning; applies both to spoken jokes and physical comedy. Timing is an aspect of delivery distinct from the text of the joke and is central to guiding narrative and eliciting laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat (purposeful pause)
rubrics_metrics.description: A beat is a pause taken for the purposes of comic timing, often to allow the audience time to recognize the joke and react, or to heighten suspense before delivering the expected punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use beats to give the audience space to process and respond; example: Jack Benny's prolonged pauses after setup lines amplify humor through audience anticipation. Beats can also heighten suspense before a punch line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnant pause (end-of-phrase pause to build suspense)
rubrics_metrics.description: A technique using pauses at the end of a phrase to build up suspense and accentuate a comedy element ('many possibilities').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used after an awkward statement or in the silence following a non-comic phrase to set up a comeback. Refined in stand-up by Jack Benny; common in stand-up routines for timing comic payoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing (slow vs fast delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall speed of delivery—slow-paced versus fast-paced—affects comedic timing and atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fast dialogue can create a frantic, silly atmosphere; slower pacing can allow jokes to land more fully. Choose pacing to support the intended mood and to manage audience reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic pauses to indicate subtext
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of dramatic pauses to distinguish subtext from spoken words or the speaker's thoughts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pauses can signal that what is unspoken or implied differs from the surface line, enhancing comedic irony or revealing hidden intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiting for laughs / including the audience in timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing involves 'waiting for the laughs' — pausing long enough for audience laughter to start and subside before moving on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the audience as an active part of the communication; do not rush into the next line before laughter has occurred or died down. Properly gauging and yielding to audience reaction is key to effective timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery elements often outweigh the written joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements like inflection, pace, and rhythm (delivery) are crucial and often more important than the written text of the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written word struggles to convey inflection and timing; successful jokes rely heavily on how they are delivered. Emphasize rehearsal and vocal/body techniques to optimize delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneous creation of timing in response to audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedians create timing spontaneously based on how they are being affected by the audience rather than possessing a fixed 'timing' trait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good timing is an act of creativity in the moment; performers should be responsive and adaptable to audience reactions, adjusting pauses and pacing dynamically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing in physical and film comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing applies to physical comedy and film performances, where beat and pacing of movement affect comedic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include silent-film comedians (Chaplin, Keaton, Laurel and Hardy) who used precise movement timing to achieve humor; choreograph physical beats and pauses as carefully as verbal timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of timing to shift tone (serious to comic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic timing (e.g., interjections, pauses) can shift the tone of a scene from serious to comic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples (Shakespeare, Aristophanes) show brief pauses or interjections transforming tone; use timing to subvert expectations and create comic contrasts within scenes.
